- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above true peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); model should adjust toward recent 7-day average if deviation > 3%.
- Model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment, high-price environments (e.g., 70–75 range with sentiment > 0.67); add 3–5% upward bias for such regimes.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67), model lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change, not wait for price confirmation.
